chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ascribed it to Amr ibn Jumay', who ascribed it to Ali (peace be upon him).
Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'and beneath it was a treasure for them'.

He said: That treasure was a tablet of gold on which was written: 'In the Name of Allah, the Merciful, the Merciful. There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. I am amazed at the one who knows that death is true, how can he rejoice? I am amazed at the one who believes in destiny, how can he store up [wealth]? I am amazed at the one who remembers the Fire, how can he laugh? I am amazed at the one who sees this world and the changing states of its people, one after another, how can he be confident in it?'
ai.seo_question: What was the treasure found beneath the wall in the story of the two orphans?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq narrates this tradition to elucidate the 'treasure' (kenz) beneath the wall in Surah Al-Kahf, identifying it as a golden tablet inscribed with profound existential reflections. The text presents four rhetorical questions that challenge human complacency regarding the certainty of death, the reality of divine decree (Qadr), the inevitability of Hellfire, and the transient nature of worldly affairs, urging believers to move from superficial joy to spiritual mindfulness.
